approve.ackRequiredBody: The plan stays pending and a reminder was sent to the employee. Try again once they have acknowledged it.

startAPPROVE.title: Approve and start this plan?
startAPPROVE.body: The plan becomes active and checkpoint tasks are created for the employee. This is recorded in the audit log.

startRETURN.title: Return this plan to draft?
startRETURN.body: The Team Lead can revise and resubmit it. The employee acknowledgement is cleared. This is recorded in the audit log.

extAPPROVE.title: Approve the extension?
extAPPROVE.body: The plan returns to active with the new end date. A plan can be extended only once. This is recorded in the audit log.

extRETURN.title: Decline the extension?
extRETURN.body: The plan returns to active with its original end date. This is recorded in the audit log.

refunds.title: Refunds
refunds.description: Each refund moves through requested, reviewed, approved or rejected, processed and reconciled, with who did it and when.
refunds.flow: Requested is not approved, and approved is not paid. The Founder or Finance approves, and Finance records the payout made outside SalesOS.
refunds.emptyDescription: Refund requests are raised from a won deal.
refunds.detailDescription: Amounts, decision trail and the next step.
refunds.missing: This refund could not be found
refunds.helpreview: Give your recommendation to the person who approves.
refunds.helpapprove: Approving does not pay anything. Finance pays out separately and records it.
refunds.helpreject: The requester is told why. This is final.
refunds.helpwithdraw: Only the requester or a Team Lead can withdraw a request that is not yet decided.
refunds.helpcancel: Cancel an approved refund that has not been paid out.
refunds.helpprocess: Record that Finance paid the refund outside SalesOS. Net collections drop only now.
refunds.helpreconcile: Match the payout with the bank statement. This locks the refund.
refunds.processNote: Do this only after the money has really been paid out. The reference must be unique.
refunds.approvedHint: Leave empty to approve the requested {amount}
refunds.amountInvalid: Enter an amount above zero with at most 2 decimals

targets.title: Targets
targets.description: Plan revenue, collection and enrolment targets and break them down from Founder to Team Lead, Manager and Executive. Nothing is edited silently: every change is a revision with a reason.
targets.noPeriodsHint: Add a month, quarter or fiscal year to start planning.
targets.noTargets: No targets for this period and metric
targets.noTargetsHint: Create the top-level target, then break it down.
targets.breakdownHint: The shares below a target can never add up to more than the target itself.

targets.pending: A revision to {amount} is waiting for approval
targets.anchorHint: Months and quarters follow the calendar; the year follows the fiscal year (April to March by default).
targets.periodHelp: Creating a period that already exists reuses it.

targets.noOwners: No active {level} found in your scope
targets.exceeds: This is more than the {left} still unallocated
targets.prorateHint: The amount is the full-period base; it is prorated by working days from the join date and the basis is stored.
targets.joinHint: For a mid-period joiner: Monday to Saturday working days are used.
targets.reviseHint: The target changes only after the right person approves. The old value stays in the history.
targets.effectiveHint: KPIs use the target in force on each date; the original is always kept.
targets.historyHint: Every value this target has had, with the reason and who approved it.

forecasts.title: Forecasts
forecasts.description: A stage-weighted estimate of revenue for the week or month. Snapshots are stored and never edited, so accuracy can be measured later.
forecasts.estimateBanner: Everything on this page is an estimate, not a fact. Real revenue is the booked sales on the Deals and Targets pages.
forecasts.bookedHint: Actual closed-won sales in the period, net of approved refunds
forecasts.weightedHint: Open deals due to close in the period times their stage probability. Unweighted: {raw}
forecasts.dealsHint: Open deals with an expected close date in the period
forecasts.noStages: No open deals in this period
forecasts.unscheduled: {count, plural, one {# open deal has no expected close date} other {# open deals have no expected close date}} ({amount}). They are not in the estimate.
forecasts.overdue: {count, plural, one {# open deal is past its expected close date} other {# open deals are past their expected close date}} ({amount}). Update the dates; they are not in the estimate.
forecasts.storedHint: Each forecast keeps its snapshots. The period-start snapshot is the one accuracy is measured against.
forecasts.noStored: No stored forecasts for this period type
forecasts.noStoredHint: Store a period-start snapshot so accuracy can be measured when the period closes.
forecasts.immutable: These values were stored at the time and cannot be changed.
forecasts.noAccuracyYet: Accuracy is calculated after the period closes.
forecasts.accuracyHint: Accuracy = 1 - |forecast - actual| / actual, never below zero. WAPE adds up the errors over the periods listed. Periods without a snapshot or with no actual revenue are not scored.
forecasts.noAccuracyRows: No closed periods to score yet
forecasts.noAccuracyRowsHint: Once a period with a stored snapshot ends, its accuracy appears here.

pricing.title: Pricing and offers
pricing.description: Price changes and offers are proposals first. Only the Founder approves them, and past sales never change.
pricing.currentHint: The latest approved price per program. Older versions are kept.
pricing.noPricesHint: Approve a price change proposal to create the first version.
pricing.proposalsHint: Draft, submitted for the Founder, approved or rejected, each with its history.
pricing.noProposalsHint: Create a proposal from what the market and learners are telling you.
pricing.missing: This proposal could not be found
pricing.noRetro: Approving a price change adds a new price version. It never changes sales that were already booked.
pricing.approveHint: A price change becomes a new price version from its effective date.
pricing.newHint: Describe the change and why. Submit it when it is ready for the Founder.
pricing.programRequired: A price change needs a program
pricing.amountInvalid: Enter an amount above zero with at most 2 decimals
pricing.rationaleHint: Refer to market, competitor or learner feedback where you can.

intel.growthNote: Estimated values are estimates only. They are not counted in revenue or forecasts.

intel.feedbackHint: Facts and quotes, not opinions about a person.

strategy.newPlanHint: A plan has a title and a summary of the approach; add initiatives afterwards.
strategy.emptyDescription: Create the first plan to track initiatives against targets.

founder.targetsHint: Achievement against the target in force, for the month, quarter and fiscal year containing the chosen date.
founder.forecastRiskHint: Open deals the forecast does not count or that slipped.
founder.teamsHint: Targets, calls, follow-ups and conversion per manager.
founder.risksHint: Everything that needs a decision or follow-up.

teamLead.scorecardsHint: Managers first, then executives. Call attempts and unique clients are shown separately.
teamLead.noLeads: No active leads in this scope.
teamLead.exceptionsHint: Every active lead should have an owner and a next action, or appear here.
teamLead.peopleHint: Counts only. Individual HR records stay in the People module.

dashboardFounder.what: The whole organisation on one screen: targets, revenue, collections, enrolments, team performance, pipeline and risks.
dashboardFounder.first: Use the period and as-of date filters at the top, then read the target tiles first. Open the risk panel for anything that needs a decision.
dashboardFounder.tip: Every number has a ? icon that shows how it is calculated. A dash means there is no data to divide by, not zero.

dashboardTeamLead.what: Sales operations across all managers and teams: targets, manager scorecards, daily activity, exceptions and ageing.
dashboardTeamLead.first: Check the exception panel first: every active lead should have an owner and a next action, or appear there.
dashboardTeamLead.tip: Call attempts and unique clients are shown separately. Calling one person three times is 3 attempts and 1 client.

dashboardManager.what: Your team's workload: each member's target, calls, follow-ups and conversion, plus overdue work and risks.
dashboardManager.first: Look at the workload panel to see who needs help before the day ends, then open their overdue tasks.
dashboardManager.tip: You only see your own team. Numbers follow the same definitions as every other dashboard.

dashboardExecutive.what: Your own workspace: your targets, activity and results. Nobody else's numbers are shown here.
dashboardExecutive.first: Start with today's callbacks and due follow-ups in Leads and CRM, call, then record the outcome.
dashboardExecutive.tip: Incentive status appears only after an incentive recommendation is approved.

dashboardAdmin.what: Shows whether the platform is running: services, job queues and data checks.
dashboardAdmin.first: Look for services marked as failing and for queues with failed jobs, then check Integrations and delivery.

crmWorkspace.what: Your day in one place: callbacks the learner asked for, follow-ups due today and the leads that need you most.
crmWorkspace.first: Work the pinned callbacks first, then today's list. Tap Call, speak to the lead, then record the outcome.
crmWorkspace.tip: Every call needs an outcome. If a lead does not answer, a retry task is created for you; the lead is never marked Lost automatically.

crmLeads.what: Search, filter and work every lead you are allowed to see.
crmLeads.first: Use the search and filters (for example Owner: Unassigned) to find leads that need attention, or add one with New lead. Open a lead to call, add notes or change its stage.
crmLeads.tip: Phone numbers are cleaned to one format. Possible duplicates are flagged for review, never merged automatically.

crmLeadDetail.what: Everything about one lead: owner, next action, call history, tasks, events and a timeline of every change.
crmLeadDetail.first: Check that the lead has an owner and a next action. Use Log call after each conversation so the next step is created.
crmLeadDetail.tip: Changing the stage or owner needs a reason where the rules ask for one, and every change is recorded in the timeline.

crmTasks.what: Every follow-up task with an owner and a due date.
crmTasks.first: Open the oldest due task, do it, then mark it done. Moving the due time restarts the reminder clock.

crmCalendar.what: Your open tasks laid out by day, in India time.
crmCalendar.first: Look at the next few days to balance your calls, and open any task to act on it.

crmOverdue.what: Tasks that passed their due time and are not done.
crmOverdue.first: Clear these before starting new work. If you cannot reach someone, log the call so a new follow-up is scheduled.
crmOverdue.tip: Owners are reminded at the due time and again after 4 hours; after one working day it goes to the manager.

crmExceptions.what: Leads that have no owner or no next action, or that need a manager's decision. This is the main safety net for lost follow-ups.
crmExceptions.first: Assign an owner and set a next action for each item. Add a note, which is saved in the audit log.
crmExceptions.tip: An empty queue is the goal: every active lead has an owner and a next action.

crmReassignment.what: Leads and tasks whose owner was deactivated and now wait for a new owner.
crmReassignment.first: Select the items, choose a new owner and give a reason. Many items can be moved at once.

crmDuplicates.what: Possible duplicate leads found by phone, email or name.
crmDuplicates.first: Open each possible duplicate, compare the details and decide. Nothing is merged unless you decide to merge it.

crmReactivation.what: Lost leads that may be worth another try, based on the lost reason and its reactivation window.
crmReactivation.first: Pick a lead and choose an owner (or leave it empty to use the team's round-robin) to reactivate it. Its history is kept.

crmImports.what: Upload a CSV of leads. Each row is checked on its own, bad rows never stop the import, and uploading the same file again does not create duplicates.
crmImports.first: Upload the file (up to 5 MB and 20,000 rows, header in the first line), check the column mapping, choose defaults, then start.
crmImports.tip: Choose Granted for consent only if you hold documented consent. Unassigned leads go to the exception queue.

crmEvents.what: Webinars and demos that your leads register for and attend.
crmEvents.first: Create a session, add or register leads, then mark attendance after it ends.

crmEventDetail.what: One webinar or demo: its status, capacity and who registered and attended.
crmEventDetail.first: Register leads here or from a lead page. After the session ends you can mark attended or no-show.

crmSettings.what: Programs, sources, stages, lost reasons, follow-up automation and round-robin for the CRM. Changes are audited.
crmSettings.first: Change only what you own. Retry delays use working hours, and team settings override the organisation settings.

revenueHome.what: Targets, deals, collections, refunds and forecasts. Sale value, money collected and money refunded are always shown separately.
revenueHome.first: Open the area you need from the tiles. Use Deals for the pipeline and Collections for money received.
revenueHome.tip: Closed-Won is not the same as payment received. A sale counts as collected only after Finance verifies the payment.

revenueDeals.what: Every opportunity from first offer to closed won or lost, with sale value kept apart from money collected.
revenueDeals.first: Open a deal to move its stage, record a payment or close it. Deals move forward only.

revenueDealDetail.what: One deal: stages, expected installments, recorded payments, adjustments and who is credited with the sale.
revenueDealDetail.first: Check the payment plan and the credit split. Closing won or lost is a separate action from moving the stage.
revenueDealDetail.tip: The booked sale value is never edited. Corrections are added as separate adjustment records.

revenueTargets.what: Plan revenue, collection and enrolment targets and break them down from Founder to Team Lead, Manager and Executive.
revenueTargets.first: Add a period, create the top-level target, then break it down. Shares below a target can never add up to more than the target.
revenueTargets.tip: Targets are never edited silently: every change is a revision with a reason, and the old value stays in the history.

revenueCollections.what: Every payment from recorded to verified to reconciled.
revenueCollections.first: Finance: verify or reject recorded payments, then reconcile against the bank or gateway statement.
revenueCollections.tip: Only verified payments count as collected money. The same transaction reference cannot be recorded twice.

revenueRefunds.what: Refund requests moving through requested, reviewed, approved or rejected, processed and reconciled.
revenueRefunds.first: Open a refund to see the amounts, who decided and the next step. Requests are raised from a won deal.
revenueRefunds.tip: Requested, approved and paid out are three different things. Nothing is paid out automatically by this system.

revenueForecasts.what: A stage-weighted estimate of revenue for the week or month.
revenueForecasts.first: Choose the period and read booked revenue first, then the weighted estimate. Store a snapshot at the start of the period.
revenueForecasts.tip: Snapshots are never edited, so accuracy can be checked honestly when the period ends.

revenuePricing.what: Price changes and offers are proposals first. Only the Founder approves them, and past sales never change.
revenuePricing.first: Write a proposal with the reason, submit it when ready, then wait for the Founder's decision.

revenueIntel.what: Log what you hear from the market, competitors and learners, and track new channels and growth ideas.
revenueIntel.first: Add feedback as facts and quotes, not opinions about a person. It feeds pricing and offer proposals.

revenueStrategy.what: Plans and initiatives for the quarter, linked to targets. Visible to managers and above.
revenueStrategy.first: Create a plan with a title and approach, then add initiatives. Team Lead and Founder can edit.

peopleHub.what: Coaching, reviews, recognition, hiring and development in one place.
peopleHub.first: Open one of the tiles. You only see what your role allows, so some areas may be missing.

peopleCoaching.what: A log of coaching sessions: date, coach, participants, topics and time spent. It records facts, not scores.
peopleCoaching.first: Add a coaching entry soon after the session while details are fresh.

peopleOneOnOnes.what: One-on-one meetings between a manager and a team member, with notes and agreed actions.
peopleOneOnOnes.first: Record the discussion and the actions you both agreed, with a due date.

peopleKpis.what: The KPIs and KRAs that define what good looks like in each role.
peopleKpis.first: Read the expectations for your role. Managers can use them in reviews.

peopleReviews.what: Performance reviews for a period, written by the reviewer and shared according to your role.
peopleReviews.first: Open a review to read or complete it. Check the period dates first.

peopleReviewDetail.what: One performance review: its period, reviewer and ratings.
peopleReviewDetail.first: Check the period and the reviewer before reading the ratings.

peoplePips.what: Supportive improvement plans with clear goals, checkpoints and approvals.
peoplePips.first: Open a plan to see its goals, checkpoints and approvals.

peoplePipDetail.what: One improvement plan: goals, checkpoints and decisions.
peoplePipDetail.first: Record each checkpoint honestly and keep notes factual.

peopleRecognition.what: Celebrate top performers and the behaviours that build the culture.
peopleRecognition.first: Give recognition with a specific reason so others can learn from it.

peopleIncentives.what: Versioned incentive policy, recommendations and the approval workflow.
peopleIncentives.first: Review the policy version first, then open a recommendation to see its status and approvals.
peopleIncentives.tip: Nothing here pays anyone. It records recommendations and approvals only.

peopleIncentiveDetail.what: One incentive recommendation: the policy version used, the calculation inputs and its approval status.
peopleIncentiveDetail.first: Check the inputs and the policy version before deciding.

peopleHiring.what: Recruitment coordination with HR: openings, candidates and interview feedback.
peopleHiring.first: Open an opening to see its candidates and interview feedback.

peopleOnboarding.what: Training checklists and probation reviews at 30, 60 and 90 days (configurable), and role expectations.
peopleOnboarding.first: Open a new joiner's checklist and tick items as they are completed.

peopleSuccession.what: Key positions and the bench of people who are ready now or ready later, with development actions.
peopleSuccession.first: Add a key position, then name successors and what each needs to grow.

peopleSkills.what: A library of coaching and skills resources for selling, leadership, communication and tools.
peopleSkills.first: Search by topic and open a resource.

peopleEngagement.what: Short anonymous surveys that show how the team is doing.
peopleEngagement.first: Answer surveys honestly. They are anonymous.

peopleEmployees.what: The minimum HR facts needed for hiring, probation and attrition reporting. Not a full HR system.
peopleEmployees.first: Search for an employee and open the record. Only people with HR permission can see this.

peopleEmployeeDetail.first: Keep the record accurate. Changes are audited.

sopLibrary.what: Playbooks and standard operating procedures for the full sales cycle.
sopLibrary.first: Search or filter for the SOP you need. Mandatory SOPs ask you to acknowledge them once you have read them.

sopReader.what: Reads the approved version of one SOP, with its change history.
sopReader.first: Read to the end, then acknowledge it if it is mandatory. Always follow the approved version.

sopEditorNew.what: Write a new SOP. Drafts are private to authors and approvers until approved.
sopEditorNew.first: Add a title and content, set who it is for, then submit the draft for approval.
sopEditorNew.tip: Use # for headings, - for lists and 1. for numbered steps. Approved versions can never be edited; make a new version instead.

sopEditor.what: Edit a draft or start a new version of an existing SOP.
sopEditor.first: Change the content, write a short change summary, then submit it for approval.
sopEditor.tip: Approved versions can never be edited. Your change summary is shown in the history.

sopDiff.what: Compares two versions of an SOP side by side.
sopDiff.first: Read the changes, then go back to the reader for the approved text.

sopAdoption.what: Who has acknowledged the current version of each mandatory SOP.
sopAdoption.first: Sort by lowest adoption and remind the people who are still pending.

sopGaps.what: A list of gaps in the sales process and the automations that would fix them.
sopGaps.first: Add a gap as soon as you find it, with a priority (P1 is most urgent). Add a resolution before marking it resolved.

sopApprovals.what: Submitted SOP versions waiting for a decision.
sopApprovals.first: Open a version, compare it with the last one, then approve or reject with a reason.

cxHub.what: Complaints, learner relationships, handovers to Student Success and Founder reporting in one place.
cxHub.first: Open the area you need. Anything overdue is shown first.

cxComplaints.what: Every complaint has an owner, a priority and a service-level clock that counts business hours.
cxComplaints.first: Log a complaint as soon as a learner raises it, send the first response, then work towards resolution.
cxComplaints.tip: A root cause is required to resolve a complaint, so the team can learn from it.

cxComplaintDetail.what: One complaint: its status, deadlines, responses and history.
cxComplaintDetail.first: Acknowledge first, then add a plan and resolve with a root cause. Escalate if you need a Team Lead or the Founder.

cxEscalations.what: High-value or complex conversations that need a Team Lead or the Founder.
cxEscalations.first: Raise an escalation with a clear request for help. Your Team Lead is notified straight away.

cxRelationships.what: See everything about a learner or prospect in one timeline, and watch key prospects.
cxRelationships.first: Search for a person, then open the timeline. You only see people you are allowed to see.

cxRelationshipDetail.what: One learner's timeline: calls, notes, stage changes, complaints, escalations, surveys and handover.
cxRelationshipDetail.first: Read from the top (newest first). Use Watch to follow this person on your watchlist.

cxSatisfaction.what: Capture CSAT, NPS and enrolment-experience scores with consent, and see the trend.
cxSatisfaction.first: Ask the learner the questions, enter their answers and confirm they agreed to feedback being stored.

cxRefunds.what: A read-only view of refunds from Revenue, with the customer-care side: root causes.
cxRefunds.first: Tag why each refund was asked for. This does not change the refund itself.

cxHandovers.what: Hand each won sale to Student Success with everything they need to welcome the learner.
cxHandovers.first: Open a handover and complete the checklist. You cannot submit until every required item is filled.
cxHandovers.tip: Student Success: acknowledge each new learner before its deadline.

cxHandoverDetail.what: One handover: the checklist, its status and the discussion between Sales and Student Success.
cxHandoverDetail.first: Fill every required item. Student Success can acknowledge, ask for more information or complete it.

cxHandoverNew.what: Start a handover for a won sale that does not have one yet.
cxHandoverNew.first: Paste the deal ID from the deal page, then complete the checklist.

cxFounderReports.what: Weekly and monthly reports for the Founder. Once published, a report is a permanent snapshot.
cxFounderReports.first: Start the report for the last completed period, fill the sections, then publish.

cxFounderReportDetail.what: One Founder report: performance, risks, opportunities and action items.
cxFounderReportDetail.first: Every risk needs a proposed solution. Publishing makes a permanent snapshot; corrections are new versions.

cxActionItems.what: Follow-ups from reviews with an owner, a due date and evidence of completion.
cxActionItems.first: Complete an item by describing what was done and giving evidence, such as a link.

cxRisks.what: Raise issues early, each with a proposed solution, before they show up in the numbers.
cxRisks.first: Add a risk as soon as you see it and say what you suggest we do.

collabTasks.what: Hand work to Marketing, Community, Operations, Student Success or the Founder with an owner, a due date and a confirmation when done.
collabTasks.first: Create a task, pick the department and the person, and set a due date. The requester confirms when it is delivered.

collabPlans.what: Line up marketing campaigns, webinars and lead generation with the sales plan, and compare planned with actual lead intake.
collabPlans.first: Link a webinar or campaign so Sales can plan follow-up capacity.

collabInsights.what: Share what you hear from learners and the market with other teams, as themes and counts, never names.
collabInsights.first: Write a short insight, tag it and choose which teams should see it.

reportingHome.what: One KPI layer feeds every dashboard, report and export, so the numbers always agree.
reportingHome.first: Choose a report from the tiles. Use the export buttons for CSV or Excel.

reportingReport.what: A report built from the same KPI definitions as the dashboards.
reportingReport.first: Set the date range and filters, read the table, then export if you need a file.
reportingReport.tip: If a report is empty, try a wider date range or fewer filters. Every export is recorded in the audit log.

reportingKpis.what: How every number is defined, with its approval status.
reportingKpis.first: Search for a KPI to see its formula, window and exclusions.

reportingReconciliation.what: Checks that dashboard totals match independent totals computed from the raw data.
reportingReconciliation.first: Run the check. Counts must match exactly and money within 0.01.

reportingExports.what: CSV and Excel files you requested.
reportingExports.first: Download a file before it expires. Large exports are prepared in the background.

adminIndex.what: Manage who can use SalesOS, how teams are organised and how the organisation is configured.
adminIndex.first: Open Users to invite or change access, or Teams to organise managers and executives.

adminUsers.what: Invite people, set their roles and keep access current.
adminUsers.first: Invite a user with a primary role, then optional secondary roles. Check the manager so team visibility is right.
adminUsers.tip: Deactivating someone ends their sessions and sends their open leads and tasks to the reassignment queue.

adminTeams.what: Teams group executives under a manager. A manager usually leads 4 to 5 executives.
adminTeams.first: Create a team, then add members. Going over the guidance only warns; it never blocks.

adminTeamDetail.what: One team: its manager and members.
adminTeamDetail.first: Add or remove members. Removing someone from the team keeps their user account active.

adminSettings.what: Defaults for teams, time and security. Changes are audited.
adminSettings.first: Change one setting at a time and check the hint under each field.

adminAudit.what: An append-only record of sensitive actions. Entries cannot be edited or deleted.
adminAudit.first: Filter by action, record type or date to find who did what and when.

adminRoles.what: A read-only view of the permission catalogue.
adminRoles.first: Use it to check what a role can do. Scope shows how far access reaches: own records, own team or the whole organisation.

adminIntegrations.what: Messaging and telephony providers, delivery history and anything that failed and can be recovered.
adminIntegrations.first: Open Needs attention to see what failed. Sent means the provider accepted a message; Delivered only after the provider confirms. Secrets are write-only and never shown again.

adminFiles.what: Limits, quotas and retention for uploaded files. Files stay private.
adminFiles.first: Change limits carefully. Files are only reachable through short-lived links after a permission check.

adminAi.what: Optional assistance for notes and follow-ups. It is off by default and the CRM works fully without it.
adminAi.first: Only turn it on after you have reviewed the privacy and consent rules.

notifications.what: Follow-ups, assignments, reviews and system alerts in one place.
notifications.first: Open an item to go straight to the work. Repeated alerts are grouped so you are not spammed.

files.what: Upload files, see how they were processed and download them.
files.first: Drag a file in or choose one. You only see files you uploaded or that are attached to records you can access.

leadOwnerNextAction.title: Owner and next action
leadOwnerNextAction.body: Every active lead needs one responsible owner and a dated next action. If either is missing, the lead appears in the exception queue.

callOutcome.title: Call outcome
callOutcome.body: Choose what really happened on the call. The outcome decides which follow-up task is created next.

callWon.title: Won
callWon.body: Use Won only when the learner agreed to buy. The value is the sale amount, not money received. Open follow-ups are closed and an onboarding task is created.

callLost.title: Lost
callLost.body: A reason is mandatory. A lead is never marked Lost just because it did not answer.

callNoAnswer.title: No answer
callNoAnswer.body: A retry task is created after the automatic delay, within working hours. The lead stays open.

leadStage.title: Stage
leadStage.body: Only valid next stages are offered. Moving backwards or reopening a lost lead needs a reason.

leadConsent.title: Consent
leadConsent.body: Withdrawn or Do-not-disturb stops reminders and outreach for this lead.

importConsent.title: Consent for imported leads
importConsent.body: Choose Granted only if you hold documented consent for these people. Otherwise leave it unknown.

importIdempotent.title: Safe to re-upload
importIdempotent.body: If an upload fails halfway, upload the same file again. Rows already imported are not duplicated.

attemptsVsClients.title: Attempts and unique clients
attemptsVsClients.body: Attempts count every call. Unique clients count each person once. Three calls to one person are 3 attempts and 1 client.

dealClosedWon.title: Closed-Won is not money received
dealClosedWon.body: Closing a deal records the sale. Money only counts as collected after Finance verifies the payment.

dealFinalValue.title: Final sale value
dealFinalValue.body: This becomes the booked sale value and cannot be edited later. Corrections are separate adjustment records.

paymentReference.title: Why a reference is needed
paymentReference.body: Enter the UTR, bank or gateway reference. The same reference cannot be recorded twice.

paymentVerified.title: Verified payments
paymentVerified.body: Recorded means someone entered it. Verified means Finance confirmed it. Only verified payments count as collected.

refundSteps.title: Refund steps
refundSteps.body: Requested, reviewed, approved or rejected, processed, then reconciled. Each step is separate and recorded.

forecastAccuracy.title: Forecast accuracy
forecastAccuracy.body: Accuracy is 1 minus the error divided by actual revenue, never below zero. Only periods with a stored snapshot are scored.

targetBreakdown.title: Breaking down a target
targetBreakdown.body: Shares below a target cannot add up to more than the target. Changing a target creates a revision with a reason.

exceptionQueue.title: Exception queue
exceptionQueue.body: Leads without an owner or next action wait here for a manager. Fixing the lead removes it from the queue.

manualCallLabel.title: Manual call record
manualCallLabel.body: This call was typed in by you. It is not verified by a phone or a provider.

handoverChecklist.title: Handover checklist
handoverChecklist.body: Fill every required item. You cannot submit until the checklist is complete.

complaintClock.title: Service-level clock
complaintClock.body: Deadlines count business hours only. Priority sets the first-response and resolution deadlines.

sopAcknowledge.title: Acknowledging an SOP
sopAcknowledge.body: Confirming you have read the current approved version. Mandatory SOPs count toward the adoption rate.

userSecondaryRoles.title: Secondary roles
userSecondaryRoles.body: These add permissions on top of the primary role. Administrators do not see HR or payment data unless it is granted.

hintsToggle.title: Hints
hintsToggle.body: Use the lightbulb in the top bar to turn all hints on or off. Reset hints in your account menu brings back dismissed page tips.
